hook.text: Odysseus tied himself to the mast to resist the Sirens. He engineered his future self's behavior. That's commitment.

buildup.text: Commitment devices are voluntary constraints you place on yourself now to prevent poor choices later.

discovery.text: StickK lets you pledge money to a cause you hate if you fail your goal. Users with financial stakes succeed 78% more.

twist.text: Commitment works because our present self can't trust our future self. Temptation degrades willpower.

climax.text: The best commitment devices make the bad choice expensive, embarrassing, or impossible. Future-you'll thank present-you.

punchline.text: Bind your future self before temptation arrives.

quiz.question: Why do commitment devices work?
options: They make poor future choices more costly, bypassing temptation
They eliminate all bad options permanently

details.summary: Commitment devices are pre-arranged mechanisms that bind people to their intended future behavior by making deviation costly or impossible. They harness present motivation to constrain future temptation, from website blockers to savings accounts with withdrawal penalties.
details.whyItMatters: Commitment devices address the gap between intention and action that plagues self-control. By creating consequences for deviation while motivation is high, they protect future behavior from the predictable erosion of willpower that undermines good.
takeaways: Commitment devices restrict future choices to prevent temptation-driven deviation
They work because people have more willpower when planning than when executing
Effective commitment devices create real costs for abandoning the committed path

faq.question: What are common examples of commitment devices?
faq.answer: Savings accounts with withdrawal penalties, website blockers during work hours, gym membership contracts, public pledges to lose weight, and alarm clocks placed across the room. Each creates a cost or barrier that makes deviation from the intended behavior harder.

faq.question: Can commitment devices backfire?
faq.answer: Yes, when they are too rigid. People who cannot meet the commitment may abandon the goal entirely rather than partially meeting it. The best commitment devices have some flexibility while still creating meaningful friction against deviation.
